changelog.change: Initial entry — converted from CV Intoxicating Substances Reference: cannabis/THC (including cannabinoid hyperemesis), synthetic cannabinoids (including brodifacoum contamination), and volatile solvents / alkyl nitrites (sudden sniffing death, methemoglobinemia).

summary: A legal low-acute-toxicity plant product and a family of synthetic analogs that are neither. Cannabis's distinctive emergencies are cannabinoid hyperemesis and prolonged pediatric edible ingestions; synthetic cannabinoids add seizures, psychosis, and — from adulteration — a superwarfarin coagulopathy. Inhalants are grouped by route: solvents sensitize the myocardium ("sudden sniffing death"), nitrites cause methemoglobinemia.
whyThisMatters: Each of these has a signature that is missed when the drug isn't asked about directly. Cannabinoid hyperemesis takes years and an expensive workup to diagnose because marijuana is "an antiemetic." Unexplained bleeding in a synthetic-cannabinoid user is a public-health outbreak pattern (brodifacoum), not a coincidence. And a pulse oximeter that reads normal on a visibly cyanotic patient is methemoglobinemia until a co-oximetry gas says otherwise.
clinicalTakeaway: Ask specifically about cannabis, "fake weed," and inhalant use — the standard cannabinoid immunoassay misses most synthetic cannabinoids, and none of these agents is volunteered as "a drug." Cyclical vomiting plus compulsive hot showers in a heavy cannabis user is cannabinoid hyperemesis (topical capsaicin, supportive antiemetics, cessation counseling). Check coagulation studies in any synthetic-cannabinoid user with bleeding — brodifacoum coagulopathy needs weeks-to-months of vitamin K1, not a single dose. In solvent abuse, avoid catecholamine stimuli and epinephrine (myocardial sensitization → VF). Trust the cyanotic patient over a normal SpO2 — send a co-oximetry gas and give methylene blue 1-2 mg/kg for symptomatic methemoglobinemia (check G6PD when feasible).

rows: Partial CB1 agonist. Concentrates (dabs, vape carts) reach 70-90% THC vs 10-25% in flower. Edibles: delayed, unpredictable onset (30-90+ min) → accidental re-dosing, severe presentations in naive users and children. Cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome — cyclical severe vomiting in a chronic heavy user, relieved by compulsive hot showers/baths (the hot-water-seeking behavior is itself a diagnostic clue)

Acute intoxication/anxiety: reassurance, low-stimulation environment, benzodiazepines for severe agitation. Hyperemesis: topical capsaicin cream to the abdomen (reasonable first-line adjunct), supportive antiemetics, IV fluids, cessation counseling (the only definitive treatment); haloperidol or benzodiazepines as adjuncts if refractory. Pediatric edible ingestion with CNS depression: supportive airway management and prolonged observation given delayed absorption
Synthetic cannabinoids (K2, Spice, "fake weed"; JWH-018, AB-CHMINACA)

Full CB1 agonists, higher affinity than THC → greater toxicity, longer duration, much higher seizure/psychosis rate. Tachycardia and seizures most common; standard cannabinoid immunoassays do NOT detect most of them. Unexplained coagulopathy with bleeding (hematuria, epistaxis, GI bleed, disproportionate bruising) = brodifacoum (superwarfarin rodenticide) contamination — a 2018 multistate outbreak

Benzodiazepines for agitation/seizures; supportive care otherwise. Check INR/PT in any synthetic-cannabinoid user with bleeding, even minor. Confirmed/suspected brodifacoum: high-dose oral ± IV vitamin K1, plus 4-factor PCC and/or FFP for active severe bleeding — then weeks-to-months of oral vitamin K1 with INR monitoring (extremely long half-life), not a one-time reversal

Nonspecific CNS depression (like an inhaled anesthetic) — but the dangerous property is myocardial sensitization to circulating catecholamines → substrate for sudden fatal VF. "Sudden sniffing death": VF cardiac arrest during/just after a session in a healthy young person, often precipitated by a catecholamine surge (being startled and running). Chronic use → metabolic/renal tubular acidosis, hepatic/renal impairment

Remove from exposure, supportive oxygen, continuous cardiac monitoring; AVOID catecholamine-driven stimuli (exertion, fright). Ventricular dysrhythmia from sensitized myocardium: avoid epinephrine/catecholamines if possible; beta-blockade has been used to blunt the sensitized response in refractory cases

Potent oxidizers — convert hemoglobin Fe2+ → Fe3+ (methemoglobin, cannot carry oxygen). Headache, syncope, and the hallmark: cyanosis and hypoxemia that does NOT correct with supplemental oxygen. Pulse oximetry reads falsely normal-ish; arterial blood is chocolate-brown

Send a co-oximetry panel (standard ABG/pulse ox will not reliably detect it). Symptomatic methemoglobinemia: methylene blue 1-2 mg/kg IV over several minutes, repeatable — check for G6PD deficiency first when feasible (methylene blue can cause hemolysis in G6PD deficiency)

body.text: A normal-looking pulse-oximeter reading does not clear methemoglobinemia — if the clinical cyanosis does not match the monitor, trust the patient and send a co-oximetry gas. And "fake weed" with unexplained bleeding is an outbreak pattern: think brodifacoum, expect a long vitamin K taper.
